title: 1978 AHSME Problem 28
statement: If \(\triangle A_1A_2A_3\) is equilateral and \(A_{n+3}\) is the midpoint of line segment \(A_nA_{n+1}\) for all positive integers \(n,\) then the measure of \(\angle A_{44}A_{45}A_{43}\) equals

solutions.text:
Let \(\mathbf d_n=\overrightarrow{A_nA_{n+1}}.\) The midpoint rule gives \(\mathbf d_{n+3}=\frac12(\mathbf d_n+\mathbf d_{n+1})\) and also \(\mathbf d_n+\mathbf d_{n+1}+\mathbf d_{n+2}=\frac12\mathbf d_n.\) Consequently, \[ \begin{aligned} \mathbf d_{n+4} &=\frac12(\mathbf d_{n+1}+\mathbf d_{n+2})\\ &=-\frac14\mathbf d_n. \end{aligned} \] Thus \(\mathbf d_{43}\) and \(\mathbf d_{44}\) are the same positive scalar multiple of \(\mathbf d_3\) and \(\mathbf d_4,\) respectively, so \(\angle A_{44}A_{45}A_{43}=\angle A_4A_5A_3.\) Since \(A_4\) and \(A_5\) are the midpoints of \(A_1A_2\) and \(A_2A_3,\) \(A_4A_5\parallel A_1A_3.\) The equilateral-triangle angles then give \(\angle A_4A_5A_3=120^\circ.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is E.
